newsitem.title: DUBAI: Rights group urges Khatami to deal with abuses.
newsitem.headline: Rights group urges Khatami to deal with abuses.

text.p: A U.S.-based human rights group has urged Iran's President-elect Mohammad Khatami to give immediate attention to alleged human rights abuses in the Islamic republic.
The New York-based Human Rights Watch made its appeal in an open letter addressed to Khatami, who takes the oath of office in parliament on Monday, and dated August 1.

"Your election, based in part on a campaign emphasising tolerance and respect for rights, creates an opportunity for the government of Iran to open a new chapter in its approach to human rights and thereby to enhance its international standing," said the letter.

"Human Rights Watch urges you to adopt a new policy of tolerance and openness towards monitoring of human rights, both by Iranians and international organisations. By allowing independent monitors into your country you will reinforce the commitment you made during the campaign to promoting rights and reining in abusive behaviour," it added.
Iran has repeatedly rejected allegations made by human rights groups on abuses in the Islamic republic.
